mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 3% over a 6-month window signals a restrictive monetary stance that raises discount rates and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the subsequent 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 3.0% and remains above for 6 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC falls below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails to activate in at least one NBER-defined recession.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase of at least 0.4 percentage points in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises by >= 0.4pp for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly below zero during triggered periods (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% over four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and prompts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines by > 1% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise of at least 3% in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) and a year-over-year increase of at least 2% in real personal income (implied by PAYEMS and CPIAUCSL) signals a housing demand recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST rises by >= 3% month-over-month AND implied real income rises by >= 2% YoY
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly above zero during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) that remains below 1% for an extended period (at least 12 months) in the absence of a simultaneous rise in inflation (CPIAUCSL < 2%) signals accommodative monetary policy that supports equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% for 12 consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL < 2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly above zero during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline of at least 0.3 percentage points in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) for four consecutive months signals a tight labor market that increases wage pressures and input costs, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to margin compression.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls by >= 0.3pp for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly below zero during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year increase of at least 4% in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) accompanied by a stable unemployment rate (UNRATE change within ±0.2pp over 12 months) signals robust aggregate demand without labor market overheating, which supports earnings growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change >= 4% AND UNRATE change within ±0.2pp for 12 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly above zero during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).
